items.evidence: python roll.py headless --ticks N --inputs SPEC [--board B] [--settings DIR] ran for all my checks; prints one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds.
--frame after headless runs on title, settings, play b1/b2/b3, paused, won, lost: all valid PNGs, IHDR 800 x 480.

python roll.py sounds judge-scratch/wav wrote 4 WAVs, identical to work/sounds: coin 0.25 s (zc 2420/s), bounce 0.18 s (167/s), fall 0.90 s (700/s), clear 0.80 s (1685/s); peaks 14k-28k, all non-silent and different.
Tick 1: screen title, selected Start. menu_down gives Settings, then Quit, then wraps to Start; down then up gives Start. Enter at tick 0 gives play, board 1, score 0, lives 3, ball at (0, 1.24, 0).

Settings opens on Volume: 8 and Language: English. 4x menu_right gives 10 (clamped); 12x menu_left gives 0; menu_right on Language gives es; two menu_lefts give en again; Enter on Back returns to the title.

With es, the texts are: title [Roll, Empezar, Ajustes, Salir]; settings [Ajustes, Volumen: 5, Idioma: Espanol, Atras]; play [Tablero 1 de 3, Puntos: 0, Vidas: 3]; paused adds [Pausa, Continuar, Salir al titulo]; won [Has ganado, Puntos: 30, Pulsa Intro...]; lost [Fin del juego, ...]. Accented letters are present; board 3 shows 'Tablero 3 de 3'.
Run 1 with --settings setP set volume 5 and es. Run 2 with the same folder starts at title with volume 5, es, Spanish texts. A run without --settings (no work/settings_data present) starts at 8, en.
Board 1, no input: y first <= 0.3 at play tick 27; bounce peaks 0.545, 0.335, 0.274; y = 0.25 at tick 600; sounds = 3x bounce.
After 30 ticks of push from rest: right +0.504 x, left -0.504 x, up -0.504 z, down +0.504 z (v 1.985). In the 30 ticks after release it moves a further 0.967 the same way, every tick.

Steered run from Title/Start (replayed by CLI, judge-scratch/b1clear.json): each coin +10 score, one coin removed, 'coin' added. The 4th coin gives board 2, 'clear' after it, ball at (-3, 1.244, 0) dropping from rest at the start, board 2's 3 coins and 6 crates in the state.
--board 2, 300 ticks with no input: 6 crates, at most 0.0004 from their brief positions, no tilt.

Push right for 70 ticks, then none: crates 2 and 5 moved 0.92 and 0.62, and the ball never reaches x = 1 (empty board: tick 87). Held push: reaches x = 1 at tick 110 vs 85 on the empty board. No crate is ever below y 0.2 while over the board.
Board 2, right held: one crate leaves past x = 4 (last seen at (6.8, -4.91, 0) at tick 231) and is removed at tick 232. The other 5 remain.

Board 1, right held: coin taken, then fall at tick 139. Lives 2, 'fall' added, ball at (0, 1.25, 0) with v = 0, taken coin stays taken. Board 2 fall to the left: crates unchanged (0.0 m). Fall on b1 then clear: board 2 with lives 2.

Board 3, '160:right,180:none': ball is at rest on the bridge at tick 361. Over the next 180 ticks its offset from bridge_x stays -0.884 to -0.862 (constant within 0.03), y 0.25, no fall. Push right at 110-170 with the bridge near x = 2: ball enters the gap at x = -0.15 (tick 201), lives 2, 'fall'.

README script --board 3 '0:right,20:none,20:right,80:none': at 1500 ticks screen won, score 30, 3 coins and 'clear'. A 2000-tick run with extra pushes/menu keys gives the same state apart from tick; enter at 2000 gives title.
--board 1 '0:right' for 900 ticks: 3 falls, screen lost, lives 0, score 10. A 1300-tick run with added left/up pushes is identical apart from tick; enter gives title.

Escape at 100 on board 2 gives paused, selected Resume. States at 101 and 600 are identical (ball, crates, score). Board 3: bridge_x stays 1.111 while paused. Enter on Resume and escape both resume play; menu_down plus enter gives title.
Two runs of board 2 with a strike (700 ticks) gave identical JSON, crates included. Two runs of the full board-1-clear script gave identical JSON.

en_b2.png: perspective view from front/above showing the whole 8x4 board, shaded round ball at the crates, 6 shaded boxes matching the state (two pushed toward +x), 3 coins. en_b3.png (bridge_x 1.67): two slabs, the gap, the blue bridge spanning about x 0.67-2.67.

Title, settings, paused and won frames show the Spanish texts, and the play HUD shows 'Board N of 3', score and lives. But the Spanish lost frame (es_lost.png) draws 'Fin del juego' too wide: its first and last letters are cut off at both edges of the 800-px frame.

gui.py:66 skips playback when volume == 0; sound.wav_bytes scales samples by volume/10 (at volume 0 the samples are all zero; at 5 the peak is 7200 vs 14400). The README says this. A headless run at volume 0 still lists bounce/coin/fall in sounds.
The README gives the keys for play, exact commands for the headless run, frame and sounds (all worked as written, including its board-3 win example), and the role of each file.

defects: The Spanish Game-over heading 'Fin del juego' is drawn wider than the 800-px frame and clipped at both sides.

After a strike on board 2, the top middle crate can come to rest (asleep) at (0.62, 0.75, 0) on a lower crate at x 0.92 whose top spans x 0.67-1.17. Its centre of mass is outside its support, so it should topple but hangs.
The window and live sound (gui.py) were never run by the builder (stated in README). The judge did not open a window either.

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
